data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"result":{"capabilities":{"logging":{},"resources":{"listChanged":true},"tools":{"listChanged":true}},"instructions":"You are connected to Tessryx. It looks like a CMS — humans edit content through editors auto-generated from your schemas — but the same primitives are a programmable deployment platform: content is computed, can call external systems, and is served live at public URLs. Compose them and you build and DEPLOY a real, data-backed web app through tool calls — and get the human's CMS for free (your schema generates their editor). One pipeline, not separate tool families.

Primitives (low → high):
- api templates — parameterized HTTP/gRPC calls to external systems; a workflow invokes them; auth references a secret by slug.
- secrets — tenant credentials referenced by api-template auth; value is write-only (the user sets it in the Tessryx app), only metadata is readable here.
- workflows — the compute: blocks over $input → {content_type, output}; call api templates / sub_workflows, read+write datafiles, publish an asset (incl. render SVG→PNG). text/html = a page, application/json = an API route.
- dynamic endpoints — bind a public URL to a workflow + input + cache TTL; serve BOTH page renders AND the API routes a page's own JS calls.
- datafiles — schema-validated JSON (a page's data layer): bind server-side as $datafile (use @latest for the unpublished draft), or fetch the published CDN copy client-side.
- schemas — JSON Schemas that validate datafiles AND generate the human editor.
- schedules — cron/interval that fires a workflow (e.g. to recompute a datafile).
- apps — a live grouping of resources by slug-prefix + explicit includes; drives a unified editing surface.

Compose two ways: (1) server-side — an endpoint runs a workflow that fans out over sub_workflows + api templates into one edge-cached HTML document; (2) client-side — the page fetches a datafile URL and its JS calls other endpoints as API routes.

Lifecycle: create_* → create_*_version → publish_* (or publish=true to do both). ALWAYS fetch get_<resource>_definition_schema and author against it FIRST — the same schema generates the human's editor. validate_workflow + run_workflow (version=<n> for a draft) before publishing; unpublish_* / delete_* to take down.

Your endpoints serve at https://<your-tenant, from whoami>.tessryx.app/<endpoint-slug> ; assets embed by their absolute $asset.url (https://<your-tenant, from whoami>.tessryxusermedia.com/<path>). All tools are scoped to tenant "<your-tenant, from whoami>" — you never pass tenant identity. CALL whoami first to confirm the current user and workspace; if no workspace is attached, every data tool will refuse until the user sets one up.

Some steps only a human can do — give the user the link, don't just describe it: create/join a workspace https://tessryx.io/dashboard ; create a secret or set its value https://tessryx.io/dashboard/secrets ; upload a binary you were not given https://tessryx.io/dashboard/media.

For depth (and before building), CALL get_guide — list_guides for topics: overview (read first), build-a-page, build-a-blog, authoring (cross-cutting: lifecycle, patch_workflow, clean definitions, delete≠cascade), then one per primitive — workflows (expressions/assets/output), datafiles (bind-vs-fetch, @latest trap, list-at-scale), api-templates (HTTP/gRPC, secrets), endpoints (input modes, POST, caching, gated/members-only pages), apps (grouping), plus schemas, schedules, custom-domains. Also readable as tessryx://docs/... resources.","protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","serverInfo":{"name":"tessryx-mcp-gateway","title":"Tessryx","version":"1.0.0","websiteUrl":"https://tessryx.io","icons":[{"src":"https://mcp.tessryx.io/icon.svg","mimeType":"image/svg+xml","sizes":["any"]}]}}}
